title.narrative: Regional Support to French/Portugese Supreme Audit Institutions

description.narrative: The main objective of this project is to improve professionalism and quality of audit work of CREFIAF member institutions on financial audits with issuance of audit opinions. The project will mainly promote (i) the actual enforcement of the professional auditing standards recently developed by CREFIAF, building on the work of the International Association of Supreme Audit Institutions (INTOSAI); and (ii) the development of a better relationship between the SAIs and external stakeholders with a view to reinforce the effectiveness of the external oversight system for public funds. The objectives pursued under this financing are in line with the ambitious CEMAC and WAEMU PFM Directives’ transposition agenda in which countries embarked on since 2009. They are also in line with the modernization of public finance legal framework in which other countries are committed to and which prescribe financial audits leading to certification of State annual accounts, assessment of public policies and performance to be carried out by Supreme Institutions of Control. It is important to note that the implementation of these Directives is supported by various World Bank technical assistance instruments (both at the national and regional level) which focus at the moment on programming, budget execution, as well as financial reporting. The proposed project will fill in the gaps in the area of external control as outlined in the implementation strategy of the Directives or the modernization of the public finance legal framework in which most countries have committed to. It also coincides with the end of the CIDA project which financed the development of audit guidelines. The preparation of this project was discussed and aligned with the AfDB (committed to performance audit) and INTOSAI, the main partners committed to support the SAIs in Africa. Likewise, the eLearning activity under this project has been discussed with UNDP which has just completed the development of an eLearning platform (http://training.le-pole.org) for Western and Central African countries on the new PFM Directives.
